note: Evaluation-only examples added to the ten project-authored seeds. Synthetic, never loaded into a real knowledge base. Roles describe why each exists.

examples.question: Which product categories have the highest return rates?
examples.method_summary: Count items with status Returned against all items that left processing, per category, over a complete window. Show both counts next to the rate so a small category with a few returns is not mistaken for a problem. Status values are current and can change.
examples.sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS items FROM sales_items GROUP BY category
examples.report_markdown:
# Return rate by category

> Synthetic retrieval-evaluation example. Illustrative method only; no figures and no real data.

examples.question: How has average order value changed month by month?
examples.method_summary: Divide completed item sales by distinct completed orders per complete month using average_order_sales v1, and compare consecutive months. Show order counts beside the average so a thin month is visible.
examples.sql: SELECT month, SUM(sale_amount) AS sales FROM sales_items GROUP BY month
examples.report_markdown:
# Average order value trend

> Synthetic retrieval-evaluation example. Illustrative method only; no figures and no real data.

examples.question: What share of purchasing customers placed more than one order?
examples.method_summary: Count purchasing customers with completed orders in the window and, within them, those with two or more distinct completed orders. Report the repeat share with both counts. Customers stay opaque references.
examples.sql: SELECT customers, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY customers
examples.report_markdown:
# Repeat purchasing

> Synthetic retrieval-evaluation example. Illustrative method only; no figures and no real data.
